verdict.rationale: Algolia's docs cover some high-availability mechanics: a retry strategy across fallback server URLs, a 99.999% uptime SLA, and an optional Distributed Search Network that routes requests to the nearest servers. Nothing in the pack documents clustering, data replication for availability, or a path to hundreds of millions of documents. The largest community-reported deployment is about 1.5M records. Missing for 10: documented clustering/sharding model, replication-for-HA documentation, an evidenced scaling path to hundreds of millions of documents, independent large-scale corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, documented scaling paths — clustering, replication, high availability — carry me from prototype to hundreds of millions of documents

citations.quote: To guarantee high availability, implement a retry strategy for all API requests using the URLs of your servers as fallbacks
If your subscription includes a Distributed Search Network, this ensures that requests are sent to servers closest to users.
